item.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
item.description:
Attorney general says ‘terrorist attack’ was attempted by suspect who is said to have been barred from flying by Oman because of extremist views The co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073 used an axe to attempt to carry out a “terrorist attack” during the Israel-bound flight, the United ⁠Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said. Disaster was narrowly averted on Wednesday when passengers and crew intervened to stop the co-pilot’s attempt to take control of the plane, which had 182 people onboard and plunged 16,625ft in just over 30 seconds. The descent was so extreme that part of the rudder was ripped off. Continue reading...

item.title: Brazil's 2026 presidential election is kicking off with polls showing Lula and Bolsonaro nearly tied.
item.description:
Brazil votes Sunday in a presidential election that could reshape its relationship with President Trump , return the Bolsonaro movement to power and alter the future of the Amazon. Why it matters: The showdown between President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Sen. Flávio Bolsonaro has turned into something bigger: a test of Trump's influence in Latin America's largest country, with stakes for the region and the global climate. The latest: Trump said Thursday he's following Brazil's election "very closely" and called it "very important," though he didn't endorse a candidate. Catch up quick: Trump inserted the U.S. into the contest when his administration imposed additional 25% tariffs on some Brazilian goods this summer — prompting Lula to accuse the American leader of "interference" in Brazil's affairs. item.title: Woman told Cornell investigators she 'felt like bait' during alleged gang rape
item.description:
People may quash their own beliefs to fit in with what they think the group believes. Andrew Lichtenstein/Corbis News via Getty Images As an undergrad student decades ago, I attended a dorm presentation describing the importance of giving and receiving sexual consent. The workshop leaders explained that if your partner said “no” or “stop” but you proceeded to have sex anyway, it was considered rape. A high-profile athlete on campus raised his hand and said, in utter disbelief, “That can’t be right. By that definition, everyone I’ve ever had sex with I’ve raped.” I was horrified by his comment, but most students laughed. He clearly saw nothing wrong with the view he’d expressed, presumably believing it was widely shared. I immediately thought of this experience when I heard about the alleged sexual assault committed by seven fraternity members at Cornell University . As a social…

item.title: Would a Firing Squad Have Been More 'Humane' for Christa Pike?
item.description:
Christa Pike, the Tennessee woman convicted of murdering Colleen Slemmer in 1995 , was a dead woman walking Wednesday. Whether or when she will walk again remains to be seen. But, as of Thursday evening, she was alive, having survived the state's attempt to execute her via lethal injection. Twice. Put differently, it did not go as planned. Correctional staff administered a (supposedly) lethal dose of pentobarbital, a barbiturate, around 7:30 p.m. "My arm feels like it's about to burst open," Pike said, according to a reporter who was there to witness the execution. Pike thrashed and did not die. So staff closed the death-chamber curtain and administered another dose, after which she began loudly snoring and struggling for air. Pike was subsequently transferred to a hospital, where she was intubated and put on a ventilator as medical personnel worked "to save [her] life," her attorneys…

item.title: In Tigray, Ethiopian government forces have advanced against a northern rebel group, reports indicate
item.description:
Ethiopian federal forces have entered the capital of the northern Tigray region and seized its airport, witnesses said Saturday, reversing a takeover by rebels from the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) that prompted the suspension of commercial flights last month. The TPLF has been fighting against pro-government forces since September 23, raising fears of an all-out civil war similar to that of 2020-2022.

item.title: North Korea launches ballistic missile after Seoul demands apology over wounded soldiers
item.description:
Pyongyang fires towards sea a day after Kim Jong-un sister denounces South Korea for claiming North’s mines wounded South’s soldiers in DMZ North Korea fired a ballistic missile towards the sea on Saturday, South Korea and Japan said, ⁠a day after it rejected Seoul’s accusation of its mines wounding soldiers. The missile was launched from the Wonsan area at about 6.30am towards the East Sea – also known as the Sea of Japan – and flew more than 700km (434 miles), the South Korean military said. Seoul and Washington were analysing the test for details, it added. Continue reading...

item.title: 'Anger in the streets': Tens of thousands protest in Spain over housing crisis
item.description:
Demonstrators take to the streets of Madrid ⁠and other Spanish cities ⁠after new legislation fails to pass Tens of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Madrid ⁠and other Spanish cities as they step up demands for action to tackle ⁠a mounting housing crisis ⁠after government measures were struck down by the opposition. Demonstrators on Saturday waved posters calling for a general strike ⁠after the measures drawn up to address mass anger over the eviction of an 87-year-old woman in ⁠Madrid, and other housing issues, were rejected in parliament on Friday. item.title: Houthis claim strike on Aramco site as Yemen fighting intensifies
item.description:
Houthi rebels accused Saudi forces of launching 26 strikes on Sanaa on Saturday after loud explosions rocked the Yemeni capital. The Iran-backed group said it struck an oil facility south of Riyadh, where flames and a large plume of smoke were seen rising from a plant belonging to oil giant Aramco.

item.title: Remains of Bulgaria’s Czar Samuel return ‘home’ after 1,000 years
item.description:
A warrior emperor who ruled the Bulgarian Empire in the Middle Ages, Czar Samuel is a symbol of Bulgarian national identity. But his remains have been in Greece for decades – and he is also claimed by North Macedonia.
